lots.what_it_is: French brass carriage clock in a corniche-style case, white enamel dial with Roman numerals, bevelled glass, folding handle, key present. The movement is stamped 'Made in France' and has two mainspring barrels and a coiled gong, with a small button on the top front. That makes it a striking clock that very likely repeats, not a plain timepiece. Unsigned, probably early to mid 20th century trade quality.

lots.guide_summary: Six Gowans SOLD hammers from $90 to $875 AUD (premium extra). The close ones are $90, $130, $260 and $550; the $875 L'Epee and the $260 two-clock lot are category guides. One UNSOLD: Roseberys passed a signed striker estimated at GBP 300 to 500 (AUD 575 to 959). No asking prices survived. Realistic hammer for this clock is about $200 to $450 if it works.
lots.working: Same-item SOLD set (close, recent, similar condition): $260 (405344, same case) and $550 (393424, with travelling case). I left out the $130 and $90 timepieces as lower spec or damaged, and the $875 L'Epee as a different maker. keep_max = 260 / 1.22 = 213.1, rounded down to $210. Flip: likely resale about $300 hammer at a Tasmanian room (between the $260 and $550 results, nudged up because it strikes). Less 15% seller commission and fees ($45), and no postage because it would be resold locally: net $255. 255 / 2.44 = 104.5, rounded down to $100. All of this assumes it runs and strikes. If it does not, it is worth about $90 to $130.
lots.confidence_reason: 'Made in France' read on the movement, and the striking train and gong are seen in the photos. Two close SOLD entries are confirmed from the Gowans API, but neither is confirmed as a striking movement, and this clock's running condition is untested.
lots.dropped_entries: John Moran 2012 'giant' repeater: HTTP 403, snippet only, 13 years old, overseas, giant size; dropped. Gumtree $1,800 ask: snippet only, from a live search page I could not verify; dropped (lead only). Gowans 406646 'Carriage clock - Made in England' $100 and 375535 Junghans $50: different makers and likely different construction; dropped. Invaluable entry moved from ASKING (USD) to UNSOLD (GBP, passed, Roseberys 2025-07-10).
lots.key_photo_findings: Back photo enlarged: 'MADE IN FRANCE' stamped on the backplate, two mainspring ratchet wheels (going and strike trains), a coiled steel gong around the backplate, and a lever at the top (probably strike or silent control). A small push button sits on the top front of the case, consistent with a repeat. Corniche-style case with a scrolled handle, bevelled glass, clean white enamel dial with no visible chips, original-looking blued hands, key present. Light wear and some tarnish on the gilt.
lots.condition: Looks good cosmetically. The dial looks clean in the photos, with light gilt wear. Running, striking and repeating are all untested.
lots.question_for_armitage: Does it run, and does it strike on the gong and repeat when the top button is pressed? Are there any hairlines or chips in the enamel dial, any cracked glass, or a mark or serial number on the backplate? What is the height?

asking.note: Page opened. 1950s Venetian dolphin-stem goblets with 24k gold in the stems and violet cups, 'some imperfections'. Available, with offers invited 5 to 15% below. AUD 3,116 for 7 (about AUD 445 each, so about AUD 1,780 pro rata for 4) at 1 USD = 1.446 AUD (open.er-api.com, 2026-10-16). A US retail ask, not a price paid, and very optimistic for an Australian auction.

lots.guide_summary: No SOLD and no UNSOLD evidence survives. The only entry is one US dealer ask (Chairish, set of 7 for US$2,155, about AUD 1,780 pro rata for a set of 4). That is retail asking only and far above any realistic Tasmanian hammer. The range shows the ask, not value.
lots.working: No SOLD evidence for dolphin-stem goblets, so both maximum bids are 0. The Gowans Venetian glass results ($10 to $50) are mixed decanter sets, not this item, and were dropped.
lots.confidence_reason: Clear identification from the photos, but there is no maker mark and the only surviving evidence is one overseas retail asking price.
lots.dropped_entries: 1stDibs set of 8 (US$3,900): page opened, but no price is shown, so the price was snippet only; it is also clear glass rather than ruby; dropped. 1stDibs single c.1915 pink-green goblet (US$1,350): page shows no price (snippet only), and it is older and finer; dropped. Gowans 378343 ($45), 435858 ($50), 405195 ($10) and 395168 ($20): confirmed in the API, but these are mixed Venetian decanter or drinks sets and generic goblets, not dolphin-stem goblets; dropped as not the same item.
lots.key_photo_findings: Four matching goblets: ruby cup, clear twisted dolphin stem with gold aventurine flecks and dark applied eyes, ruby foot. The stems vary a little, as hand-made pieces do. No chips, cracks or labels visible in the two photos, and no acid mark or label seen.
lots.condition: Looks good in the photos, with no visible chips. The rims and feet need checking by hand.
lots.question_for_armitage: Any chips or flea bites on the rims or feet, or cracks at the stem joins? Any Murano or Salviati label or acid mark under the feet? What is the height of each goblet?
